keyFindings.finding: Single-provider dependency is the #1 availability risk; every major LLM provider had multi-hour outages in the last 12 months.
keyFindings.evidence: OpenAI had 3 outages in Q2 2025 alone; Anthropic June 2026 outage took down Claude globally; Thoughtworks labeled it 'infrastructure reckoning'.

keyFindings.finding: A gateway/abstraction layer is the standard pattern — not per-service fallback logic.
keyFindings.evidence: TrueFoundry, Portkey, LiteLLM, Router One, Azure APIM, and custom adapters all converge on the AI Gateway pattern.

keyFindings.finding: Fallback chains across providers give independent failure domains; within-provider failover shares failure domains.
keyFindings.evidence: Cross-provider (Claude → GPT → Gemini) vs within-provider (alternate region) — both useful, different guarantees. Cross-provider is essential for provider-wide outages.

keyFindings.finding: Latency-based failover catches more real-world degradation than error-code-based failover.
keyFindings.evidence: Velorith: '3-5 consecutive slow responses before switching prevents thrashing'; degrade trends justify routing around before requests fail.

keyFindings.finding: Circuit breakers prevent cascading failures by stopping traffic to degraded providers.
keyFindings.evidence: Sierra uses AIMD admission control; Portkey/TrueFoundry use sliding window error rate; Azure APIM uses consecutive failure threshold.

keyFindings.finding: Not all errors should trigger fallback — 4xx errors (auth, bad request) fail universally; only 5xx, network errors, timeouts, and 429 rate limits should trigger.
keyFindings.evidence: Consensus across Router One, NiteAgent, Portkey, and DevOpsNess guides.

keyFindings.finding: Output variance across models is the biggest hidden risk — 'comparable on leaderboard ≠ comparable on my prompt'.
keyFindings.evidence: Indra Gusti Prasetya: golden eval gating required before a fallback serves traffic; same-family failover (GPT→GPT) preserves behavior, cross-family needs validation.

keyFindings.finding: Per-task routing reduces cost by 30%+ while improving resilience.
keyFindings.evidence: DevOpsNess: 'route simple tasks to cheaper models'; NiteAgent: 50-70% of requests can land on GPT-4.1 Nano or Haiku instead of GPT-4o, saving 96% on that tier.

keyFindings.finding: Fallback providers must be kept warm with canary traffic to avoid cold-start latency.
keyFindings.evidence: Hyperion: 'If secondary hasn't seen traffic in weeks, first failover may suffer latency spikes'; send 1% production traffic to fallbacks constantly.

keyFindings.finding: Streaming (SSE) failover cannot be handled at the gateway level — requires client-side retry.
keyFindings.evidence: AWS SnapSoft + Azure APIM guides both note: gateway cannot failover mid-stream; client must handle interrupted streams with retry.

keyFindings.finding: Model deprecation is a separate failure mode from outages — needs calendar-based migration pipeline plus a kill-switch path.
keyFindings.evidence: Indra Gusti Prasetya: 'Two clocks — one scheduled deprecation, one fire drill'; Opus 4.1 retirement date augurs proactive migration.

architecturePatterns.description: Central layer that owns provider selection, retries, fallbacks, circuit breaking, cost tracking, observability
Tier 1: Frontier model primary → Tier 2: Cheaper/available comparable → Tier 3: Deterministic template/rule → Tier 4: Async recovery / human escalation
Route by task capability: classification → small/cheap, reasoning → frontier, safety → strict model. Each task has its own primary + fallback list.
implementations: Sierra MMR enforced per-task model list

architecturePatterns.description: Track error rate on sliding window; open circuit when threshold exceeded; half-open probes; auto-close on recovery
Normalizes tool schemas, strips unsupported params, reconciles structured-output mechanics per provider
Send request to primary, fire identical request to secondary if no response within tight deadline; use whichever responds first
Route small % (e.g. 1%) of traffic to fallback providers constantly to keep them warm and measure real latency

statistics.outageImpactAvoidance: 92% of provider outage impact avoided with fallback chains (NiteAgent/TrueFoundry data)
statistics.costSavings: ~30% from per-task routing; up to 96% on classification tier by using smaller models
statistics.fallbackIncidence: 0.5-2% of requests hit fallback under normal conditions, spikes during provider incidents
statistics.handoffOverhead: Under 200ms added per fallback hop through gateway (Router One data)
statistics.simpleRequestShare: 50-70% of requests can land on cheaper models without quality loss

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.strengths: Order-based priority routing, cooldowns, num_retries with backoff, wide provider support
tools.weaknesses: Less mature streaming support, additional infrastructure to run

tools.name: Portkey AI Gateway
tools.strengths: Conditional fallback by status code, virtual keys, request tracing, 4xx/5xx code-based switching

tools.name: TrueFoundry AI Gateway
tools.strengths: Fallback chains, health-aware routing, per-request retry policy, streaming support

tools.name: Azure API Management
tools.strengths: Deep Azure integration, circuit breaker policies, multi-region, 429-aware retry
tools.weaknesses: Azure-only, complex policy XML, can't failover mid-stream

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.strengths: Single API, basic fallback routing, no infra to manage
